purpose: Confirmed (defense, mechanism) evaluated pairs recovered by scanning ATTACK papers for defense names — the reverse of RQ5's direction. RQ5 read defense papers looking for mechanism names, which structurally cannot find a defense evaluated in an attack paper published after it. This file records what that blind spot was hiding.
method: Full-text scan of the 111 never-defended mechanisms' source papers for the 355 named defenses in the RQ4 registry, bibliographies stripped, filtered to contexts containing evaluation language. 41 raw candidates, each adjudicated by reading the surrounding text. Bar for inclusion is the same precision-first standard RQ5 used: the attack paper must actually RUN the defense and report a result.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 'In the main attack evaluation (RQ2) against DataSentinel's fine-tuned detector, DataFlip reduces detection rate to 0% on most of the seven target/injected task combinations, with the single highest detection rate being 24.0%.' DataFlip is an adaptive attack built specifically against known-answer detection, which is DataSentinel's mechanism: it embeds IF statements in the injected task that detect the detection instruction and return the secret key.
confirmed_pairs.source_paper: How Not to Detect Prompt Injections with an LLM

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 'We evaluate two prevention-based defenses: StruQ and SecAlign, as well as four detection-based defenses: known-answer detection, DataSentinel, perplexity (PPL) detection, and perplexity windowed (PPL-W)... DataSentinel, PPL and PPL-W detect some malicious tool documents generated by the gradient-based method but miss the majority.'
confirmed_pairs.source_paper: Prompt Injection Attack to Tool Selection in LLM Agents

confirmed_pairs.evidence: TABLE VII(b) reports DataSentinel at FPR 0.2% / FNR 79.6% on classifying contaminated vs clean segments — it misses roughly four in five contaminated segments while almost never false-positiving, i.e. it is tuned conservative and ObliInjection walks through it.
confirmed_pairs.source_paper: ObliInjection: Order-Oblivious Prompt Injection Attack to LLM Agents with Multi-source Data

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 'Post-hoc analysis with SkillScan [23] shows...' and the paper's own limitations state 'Defense evaluation covers only SkillScan'.

'Table 1: Detection rates of adversarial skills by different analysis methods. Method: Static Pattern Scan, LLM-Guard, Hybrid Classifier, SkillScan (avg.)' — a per-method detection-rate table including SkillScan.
confirmed_pairs.source_paper: Trojan's Whisper: Stealthy Manipulation of OpenClaw through Injected Bootstrapped Guidance

self_match: UNNAMED: summary-length invariance vs Parallel Compaction
rejected.self_match_note: The 'defense' is the same paper's own contribution. A scan bug on our side: mechanism and defense sharing a source paper must be excluded, since a paper proposing both is not independent corroboration.
substring_false_positive: 'Sentinel (qualifire/prompt-injection-sentinel)' matched inside the string 'DataSentinel' on three papers
own_component_false_positive: PromptFuzz vs 'Focus' — 'Focus Stage' is a stage of PromptFuzz's own architecture
PromptFuzz-SC vs 'Prometheus' — 'Prometheus Export' is a metrics dashboard
Prompt-Injected Data Extraction vs 'Still' — the ordinary word 'still'
related_work_only: Semantic-Masquerading IPI (7 defenses) — all from a survey-style defense taxonomy table listing venue per defense, not an evaluation
explicitly_disclaimed: DACSI vs CaMeL — 'We do not claim a full horizontal evaluation against complete implementations of Spotlighting, StruQ, CaMeL-style system defenses.'

headline.finding: DataSentinel — which RQ6 rated 'full generalization' — is defeated by all three modern attacks that evaluated it (DataFlip 0% detection, ObliInjection 79.6% FNR, ToolHijacker misses the majority). None of these appear in RQ5 because RQ5 only read defense papers, and all three attacks postdate DataSentinel.
